transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… it’s this thing at work. If I even think there might be a bat, or something flapping around in the stockroom, I kind of panic right away. My heart jumps, I start sweating, and I just feel like I need to get out of there.
Is it just bats that trigger this panic, or are there other things that can cause a similar reaction?
Mostly bats, or… anything that seems like one. Like if I catch a quick flutter in the back hallway, even if I know it’s probably nothing dangerous, my head just reacts like it is.
Do you ever have these panic episodes when you're not thinking about bats or something flapping around?
No… not really. It’s usually right when I think there might be a bat or something flapping around. Then it hits fast—my heart jumps, I sweat, and I just want to get out.
Do these panic episodes only happen when you're at work or can they occur in other locations as well?
I’m not really sure. I notice it mostly at work, just because that’s where it comes up. I haven’t paid much attention anywhere else.
Do you think you would have this panic reaction if you saw a bat in a different context, like in a movie or a picture?
Maybe… I’m not totally sure. A picture probably not the same, but if it seemed real or something was flapping, then yeah, I think I’d get that quick jolt and want to get away.
Do you think you would have this panic reaction if you saw a bat at home?
Yeah… I think so. If I thought there was a bat in the house, or something flapping around, I’d probably get that same rush and want to get out right away.
Do you think you would have this panic reaction if you were in a completely safe and controlled environment, like this office, and someone just mentioned the word 'bat'?
Probably not just the word, no. I mean… it’s more if I think there might actually be one, or something flapping around. Then my heart kind of jumps and I feel like I need to get out.
Do you think the panic reaction would happen in any situation where you thought there might be a bat, regardless of where you are?
Yeah… I think so. If I really thought there might be one there, wherever I was, I’d get that same sudden jump, start sweating, and just feel like I needed to get away right then.
Is there anything else, besides bats or things that seem like bats, that you are afraid of?
Not really. I mean… nothing that comes to mind like that. It’s mostly just bats, or stuff I mistake for them.
Are you afraid of any other animals besides bats?

No, not really. I know a bat probably isn’t going to hurt me, like if it was in the store or something… but if I see a quick flutter or something that looks like one, my mind just treats it like danger. Other animals don’t really do that.
Do you think your panic reaction to bats is because of something about the bats themselves or because of the unexpected or sudden movement they represent?

I guess it’s more the bat itself… or what I think is a bat. Like, I know if one was in the store it probably wouldn’t hurt me, but if I see a quick flutter in the back hallway, my mind just reacts like it’s real danger.
Is there anything else, besides bats, that you fear might be present in a situation and triggers a similar panic reaction?
No… not really anything else. It’s more if I think it could be a bat, like a quick flutter back in the hallway. Even though I know it probably wouldn’t hurt me, my head reacts like it’s danger.
Would you have a similar panic reaction if you thought there might be another type of animal, like a snake or a spider, in the same situation?

No… I don’t think so. If it was a snake or spider, I mean, I wouldn’t like it, but it’s not the same. It’s really when I think it might be a bat—like a quick flutter in the back hallway. My head just treats it like real danger, even though I know it probably isn’t.
Would your panic reaction be the same if you thought there might be any other animal in the room, not just a bat?

No… not the same. It’s really bats, or if I think something might be one. Like a quick flutter in the back hallway—I know it probably wouldn’t hurt me, but my mind just reacts like it’s serious danger.
Do you think you would have this panic reaction if you were alone at home and thought there might be a bat present?
Yeah… if I was alone and thought there might be a bat, I’d probably panic pretty fast. My heart kind of jumps, I start sweating, and I just feel like I need to get out right away.
Does the panic reaction to bats happen at night or is it more of a daytime thing?
I’m not really sure… I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s night or daytime. It’s more just if I think one might be there.
Do you ever have these panic episodes unexpectedly, without thinking about bats or being in a situation where you might see one?
I don’t think so… not really. It’s usually when something makes me think of bats or that one might be around.
Is there anything else, besides bats, that you fear or dislike intensely?
Not really… I mean, there are things I don’t like, but nothing that gets to me like bats do.
Do you typically have a panic episode without any apparent trigger or warning, separate from thinking about bats?
No… I don’t think so. It’s usually tied to bats somehow, or thinking there might be one.
